title: Meeting Your Neighbor
objectives: Use simple 'to be' sentences (I am, you are)
Have a basic first conversation in English

phrases: I am good / I am fine
target_language.grammar_pattern:
I am [name]
I am from [place]
I am good

You are [name]
You are from [place]
You are good

Examples:
- I am Ahmed
- I am from Somalia
- You are Marcus
- You are from America

story.context: You are in the hallway of your apartment building. A man comes out of the apartment across from yours.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: My name is Ahmed. I am from Somalia. I live in 4B.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I am good. Thank you. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: I'm good. Welcome to the building!

drills.title: Drill 1: Substitute the name
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct name
drills.your_turn: Now say 'My name is [YOUR NAME]' out loud and record it

drills.title: Drill 2: Substitute the place
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct country
drills.your_turn: Now say 'I am from [YOUR COUNTRY]' out loud and record it

drills.title: Drill 3: Complete introduction
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank to complete the introduction

prompts.sentence: Hi. My name is Marcus. I am from ___.
Hi. My name is Sarah. I am from ___.
Hi. My name is ___. I am from Somalia.
Hi. ___ name is Fatima. I am from Kenya.

examples: Hi. My name is Marcus. I am from America.
Hi. My name is Sarah. I am from England.
Hi. My name is Ahmed. I am from Somalia.
drills.your_turn: Now introduce yourself completely out loud (Hi + name + where you're from) and record it

listening.question: Listen: What is her name?
listening.transcript: Hello. My name is Sarah. Nice to meet you.

listening.question: Listen: Where is he from?
listening.transcript: Hi. My name is Marcus. I am from America.

listening.question: Listen: How is she?
listening.transcript: Hello. How are you? I am good, thank you.

speaking.title: Task 1: Introduce yourself
speaking.instruction: Record yourself saying: 'Hi, my name is [YOUR NAME]. I am from [YOUR PLACE].'
speaking.example: Hi, my name is Ahmed. I am from Somalia.

speaking.title: Task 2: Complete conversation
speaking.instruction: Imagine you meet Marcus. Record the full conversation from the story. You are 'You' in the dialogue.
speaking.example:
Person A: Hi!
Person B: Hello. My name is Ahmed. I am from Somalia.
Person A: Nice to meet you!
Person B: Nice to meet you too.

writing.title: Task 1: Fill in the blanks
writing.example:
1. My name is _____.
2. I am from _____.
3. I am _____. (good/fine/great)

writing.title: Task 2: Write a conversation
writing.instruction: Write a short conversation (6-8 lines) where two people meet for the first time. Use the phrases from this lesson.
writing.example:
Person A: Hi!
Person B: Hello.
Person A: My name is Sarah. I am from England.
Person B: Nice to meet you! My name is Ahmed.
Person A: Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
Person B: I am from Somalia.
Person A: How are you?
Person B: I am good. Thank you.

sections.title: Look at these sentences:
sections.question: What do you notice? What comes after 'I'?
sections.explanation: All three sentences use 'I am'. We use 'I am' to tell people about yourself.

sections.title: Now look at these:
sections.question: What is different from the first group?
sections.explanation: When talking to someone else, we use 'you are' instead of 'I am'.

sections.title: What can come after 'I am' or 'you are'?
sections.question: Can you think of other things that could come after 'I am'?
sections.explanation: You can use 'I am' with your name, where you're from, how you feel, and many other things about yourself.

quiz.question: How do you tell someone your name?
quiz.explanation: We say 'My name is [name]'. This is the natural way to introduce yourself.

quiz.question: Someone says 'Nice to meet you.' What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'Nice to meet you too' is the standard, polite response.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: I ___ from Somalia.
quiz.explanation: We use 'am' after 'I'. So it's 'I am from Somalia.'

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: You ___ Marcus.
quiz.explanation: We use 'are' after 'you'. So it's 'You are Marcus.'

quiz.question: When Marcus says 'How are you?', what does he want to know?
options: How you feel / if you are okay
quiz.explanation: 'How are you?' is asking about how you feel or if you are doing well.

quiz.question: You want to ask about someone's feeling or condition. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'How are you?' is the standard question to ask about someone's well-being.

quiz.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
quiz.explanation: The correct form is 'I am from Somalia'. We need 'am' after 'I'.

quiz.question: What does 'Hi' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Hi' is an informal way to say hello and greet someone.

quiz.question: Write a 4-line conversation where you meet someone named Sarah from England. Use the phrases you learned.
quiz.explanation:
Your conversation should include greetings, names, and where you're from. Example:
Sarah: Hi! My name is Sarah.
You: Hello. My name is Ahmed.
Sarah: Nice to meet you. I am from England.
You: Nice to meet you too. I am from Somalia.

quiz.question: Think about the lesson. Write 2-3 sentences: What was the most useful phrase for you? Why?
quiz.explanation: There is no wrong answer. This helps you reflect on what you learned and what will be most useful in your life.
